html:
The Meherrin, who call themselves Kauwets'a:ka, are an Iroquoian-speaking people of the Meherrin River on the border of Virginia and North Carolina. Their language was close to that of the Nottoway and the Tuscarora.

They lived in palisaded towns, farmed maize and hunted, and traded with English colonists from Virginia from the mid 1600s. As settlers pressed in, they moved south down the river into North Carolina.

After the Tuscarora War of 1711 to 1715 they lost much of their land to settlers in the following decades. Their descendants form the Meherrin Indian Tribe, recognised by North Carolina in 1986.
